headline: BoC Set to Hold at 2.25% on June 10 as May Employment Rebounds 88,000 and Q1 GDP Slips to Flat
executive_summary:
The Bank of Canada heads into its June 10 decision with the overnight rate at 2.25%55 and a five-week-old hold to defend. The Bank Rate stands at 2.50% and the deposit rate at 2.20%, unchanged since the April 29 fixing.55 The cross-reference engine links the rate hold to 722 active power and energy projects ($486.15B) and 231 active residential and housing projects ($36.27B)54 whose financing structures track the policy path.

Statistics Canada's May Labour Force Survey recorded employment +88,000135 and unemployment down 0.3 percentage points to 6.6%, a swing of +115,500 from April's -27,500 print.135 Gains concentrated in construction (+27,000), transportation and warehousing (+19,000), information, culture and recreation (+19,000), accommodation and food (+17,000), and manufacturing (+15,000).135 The database tracks 964 active infrastructure projects ($200.04B), 468 transport/transit projects ($34.41B), and 79 manufacturing projects ($69.46B)54 in the sectors carrying the rebound.

Real GDP was flat at 0.0% q/q in Q1 2026 after a revised -0.2% q/q in Q4 2025; per-capita GDP rose +0.2% q/q as population fell for a second consecutive quarter.133 Headline CPI accelerated to +2.8% YoY131 in April from +2.4% in March, driven by gasoline +28.6% YoY; core trim sat at 2.0% and core median at 2.1%, both five-year lows.131 The federal fuel excise tax suspension effective April 20 dampened the pump-price print.18

The Carney government's Spring Economic Update establishes the $25B Canada Strong Fund — the first national sovereign wealth fund — and the $51B Build Communities Strong Fund over 10 years.67 USD/CAD reached an 8-week high of 1.3949 on June 7 after US payrolls of +172,000 beat the +85K consensus63, and the TSX Composite fell 2.28% to 34,413 on June 5.60 Statistics Canada releases April merchandise trade on June 9, the BoC decision lands June 10, and the ECB Governing Council meets June 11 with markets pricing a 99% probability of a +25 bps move to a 2.25% deposit rate.35

provinces.analysis:
Ontario's unemployment rate fell 0.5pp to 7.0%79 in the latest reading, still 0.4pp above the 6.6% national rate, while real GDP held at +1.2% year-over-year19. The province's labour-force participation rate eased 0.1pp to 64.7% and the employment rate added 0.3pp to 60.2%79. Housing starts held at 62,735 (annualized) in the latest CMHC print.

The province's 2026 Budget commits more than $210B over 10 years to infrastructure, including $37B in 2026–27 across highways, hospitals, transit and community infrastructure, against a projected $13.8B deficit returning to surplus by 2028–2981. The tracked Ontario pipeline contains 728 projects valued at $448.9B, with infrastructure (204 projects) and Under Construction status (267 projects) the largest cohorts. The Ring of Fire all-season road is scheduled to start construction in June 2026 with road opening November 2030, five years ahead of the prior schedule12.

Health infrastructure adds another tranche: roughly $64B over a decade, including about $50B in capital grants, ~50 hospital projects and ~3,000 new beds73. Newly tracked Ontario projects this cycle include the Canada National AI Strategy ($2.3B Proposed), the Ontario Higher Education Sector Funding Program ($1.7B Proposed), and the Sunnybrook Health Sciences Centre $1B Capital Campaign (Proposed) — the Sunnybrook figure is a campaign goal, not a committed project value, and is flagged as such in the underlying dossier.

The province's CPI series returned +6.8% year-over-year in the StatCan WDS pull, materially above the +2.8% national headline19. If the series is confirmed, the print would mark a substantial divergence from the national basket; the figure is preserved here unaltered but is flagged for verification against StatCan Table 18-10-0004 before any policy or project linkage is drawn.

provinces.analysis:
Quebec posted the lowest unemployment rate among the four largest provinces at 5.6%98, down 0.6pp from the prior period and 1.0pp below the 6.6% national rate. Real GDP held at +1.3% year-over-year19 and CPI of +1.5% tracked well below the +2.8% national headline79. Participation eased 0.3pp to 64.1% while the employment rate added 0.2pp to 60.6%.

The federal-Quebec Canada-Quebec Infrastructure Partnership was signed 2026-06-02, committing roughly $10B over 10 years: about $6B in public transit (including TramCité), $1B in hospital renovations by 2028–29, $2.7B for higher education, $400M for transit electrification, and more than $2.5B through the Build Communities Strong Fund81. The Quebec pipeline carried three near-duplicate $10B entries for this agreement; the underlying dossier collapsed them to one canonical entry. The tracked Quebec pipeline spans 509 projects valued at $107.9B, with education (118 projects) and Approved status (300 projects) the largest cohorts.

The Hydro-Québec Gull Island and Churchill Falls document disclosure dispute with Newfoundland and Labrador escalated ahead of next-step bargaining on the December 2024 AIP — 2,250 MW new plant commissioning 2034, 1,100 MW Churchill Falls extension 2035, and 550 MW through turbine-generator upgrades12. The Quebec health minister is set to table legislation restricting teen energy-drink sales73. Provincial macro timeseries (qc_exports, qc_imports, qc_business_investment, qc_real_gdp, qc_bldg_permits, qc_retail_sales, qc_manufacturing_sales, qc_housing_starts) are 99–250 days stale per the data gap report and are not anchored here.

CPI of +1.1% ties Saskatchewan for the lowest provincial print and sits 1.7pp below the +2.8% national headline79.

The Alberta Energy Regulator forecast oilsands production growth of more than 17% by 2033, reaching approximately 4.0 mbpd from 3.4 mbpd12. The tracked Alberta pipeline spans 717 projects valued at $370.6B, with government (143 projects) and Proposed status (372 projects) the largest cohorts — the deepest Proposed bench of any region. The Oil Sands Alliance reaffirmed its commitment to the Pathways Alliance CCS project conditional on regulatory and fiscal terms, following the May 2026 Canada-Alberta bilateral on revised industrial carbon tax mechanics tied to the November 2025 MOU baseline81.

Telus Infrastructure Upgrades ($19.0B Under Construction) remains the largest single tracked entry in the province. Newly tracked Alberta IAAC entries first registered 2026-06-08 include the OS-6891 and OS-6908 oilsands surface lease authorizations. Alberta is one of seven signatories — alongside BC, SK, MB, YT, NT and NU — to the Western Canadian Critical Minerals Strategy, with the final strategy expected at the 2026 Energy and Mining Ministers Conference73. WTI and WCS price moves flow through to Alberta's oil_gas project breakeven thresholds against the 26 oil_gas projects in the tracked cohort.

provinces.analysis:
Newfoundland and Labrador's unemployment rate of 9.6% is the highest provincial print and sits 3.0pp above the 6.6% national rate73. Employment rate of 51.3% is the lowest provincial print; participation of 56.7% is the second-lowest after NB. Housing starts held at an annualized 1,242 in the latest CMHC reading.

The Independent Churchill River Review Committee report was released, with more than 350 submissions received between 2025-12-16 and 2026-04-30 on the December 2024 NL Hydro–Hydro-Québec AIP — 2,250 MW new plant commissioning 2034, 1,100 MW Churchill Falls extension 2035, and 550 MW added via turbine-generator upgrades81. The tracked NL pipeline spans 1,543 projects valued at $26.7B — the second-highest provincial count after Manitoba — with Proposed (1,358 projects) dominating the status mix, reflecting ECCC project registry capture.

Hydro-Québec sought to withhold documents from the NL government per a National Observer report, ahead of next-step bargaining on the AIP81. Grassy Point LNG ($10.0B Proposed) remains the largest single tracked entry; the Kamistiatusset (Kami) iron ore project ($3.9B Under Review) and the White Rose Expansion (West, $3.8B Under Construction; North/South, $2.3B Under Construction) anchor the in-flight offshore-oil and mining cohorts.
